instruction: Start VS Code and load the project located at /home/user/project/ so its files appear in the file explorer.

command: cd /home/user/Downloads && unzip -q vscodeEvalExtension.zip && code --install-extension vscodeEvalExtension/eval-0.0.1.vsix && rm -rf vscodeEvalExtension vscodeEvalExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening VSCode and loading the project folder so that the file explorer displays the project files (main.py, README.md, and .vscode directory). The evaluator uses a custom VSCode extension command 'GetExplorer' to retrieve the explorer content and checks if all expected files are visible. Score is proportional to how many files are found (0.33 per file). Verified that the project contains these 3 items based on the cache files read.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies instruction requirement: checks if VSCode explorer shows the expected project files (main.py, README.md, .vscode)
Getter logic is appropriate: uses VSCode extension command 'GetExplorer' to capture explorer state to a file
Metric logic is sound: reads the explorer output and checks for presence of all expected files using substring matching
Complete coverage: all 3 expected files/folders are checked with proportional scoring (0.33 per file) for partial credit
Expected values are correct: verified based on the project files downloaded in config (main.py, README.md, .vscode/settings.json)
Postconfig is present and appropriate: activates VSCode window before running verification
Data flow is correct: getter extracts explorer state → writes to file → metric reads file and validates file presence
Minor issue: metric uses simple substring matching which could have edge case false positives, but for this specific task (checking top-level explorer files) it should work correctly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider more robust file matching: instead of simple substring match, could parse the explorer output more carefully to distinguish between file/folder names vs. paths containing those names
Consider adding metric parameter name consistency: parameter is named 'rules' instead of standard 'expected', though this doesn't affect functionality
